title: Electrochemical sensing of cell viability: A scalable platform from 2D monolayers to 3D tissue models

figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Cyclic voltammetry scans of various cell culture media components using SPCEs in a three-electrode configuration(A) Phosphate buffered saline (PBS), (B) DMEM medium, and (C) EpiLife medium. All scans were performed at a scan rate of 50 mV/s. The absence of distinct oxidation or reduction peaks across the potential range (−0.6 to +0.7 V) confirms the electrochemical inertness of these media, ensuring no interference with subsequent MTS signal detection.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Cyclic voltammetry of MTS samples reduced with different NADH concentrations, performed using SPCEs at a scan rate of 50 mV/s(A) The complete cyclic voltammograms demonstrating the presence of a current peak in the cathodic scan, located between −0.3 and −0.1 V (indicated by the red square), corresponding to the electrochemical signal of reduced MTS (formazan).(B) A magnified view of the potential region where the MTS signal is detected. This zoomed-in section illustrates the concentration-dependent increase in the absolute current magnitude as NADH concentration, and consequently, the amount of reduced MTS increases. Plotted data represent the mean value of each repetition (n = 7).

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Correlation analysis of MTS reduction by NADH in EpiLife and DMEM culture media(A) Mean absorbance (OD) as a function of NADH concentration in EpiLife medium (conventional spectrophotometric method, R2 = 0.9522).(B) Electrochemical current intensity peak as a function of NADH concentration in EpiLife medium (proposed electrochemical method, R2 = 0.9493).(C) Mean absorbance (OD) as a function of NADH concentration in DMEM medium (conventional spectrophotometric method, R2 = 0.9486).(D) Electrochemical current intensity peak as a function of NADH concentration in DMEM medium (proposed electrochemical method, R2 = 0.9667).(E) Correlation between mean absorbance (OD) and electrochemical current intensity peak in EpiLife medium (R2 = 0.9327).(F) Correlation between mean absorbance (OD) and electrochemical current intensity peak in DMEM medium (R2 = 0.9023). Data are represented as mean ± standard deviation (SD) for n = 7 replicates.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: Comparison of the percentage error in MTS reduction measurements obtained via the electrochemical signal versus absorbance readings in EpiLife and DMEM culture mediaBar graphs represent the mean percentage error, with individual data points overlaid. Error bars indicate standard deviation. The electrochemical measurements consistently demonstrated significantly lower variability and greater precision compared to the conventional spectrophotometric method. Statistical significance is denoted by ∗∗ (p < 0.01, derived from one-way ANOVA).

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.caption: Quantitative assessment of MTS reduction in human dermal fibroblast (hDF) cell confluency after a 3-h incubation with the MTS reagent(A) Linear correlation between cell confluency percentage and mean MTS absorbance (OD) as measured by the conventional spectrophotometric method (R2 = 0.9684).(B) Linear correlation between cell confluency percentage and electrochemical current intensity peak measured by the proposed sensor (R2 = 0.9358).(C) Correlation between the electrochemical current intensity peak and the spectrophotometric mean absorbance (OD) (R2 = 0.9056).(D) Electrochemical current intensity in cells treated with NADH-oxidase and its corresponding control with DMSO.(E) Electrochemical signal response in cells treated with NADH-oxidase and its corresponding control (DMSO). The significant reduction in the peak current upon NADH inhibition confirms the metabolic origin of the formazan-derived signal. All data are represented as mean ± standard deviation (SD) for n = 7 replicates.

figures.label: Figure 6
figures.caption: MTS reduction measurements in hDFs and N/TERT-1 keratinocytes after chemical exposure after a 3-h incubation with the MTS reagent(A) Electrochemical current intensity in hDFs and (B) corresponding MTS absorbance in hDFs. (C) Electrochemical current intensity in N/TERT-1 keratinocytes and (D) corresponding MTS absorbance in N/TERT-1 keratinocytes. Chemicals tested include PBS (negative control, C−), 1-bromo-4-chlorobutane, isopropanol, 1-decanol, 5% aq. KOH, and 5% aq. SDS (positive control, C+). Data are represented as mean ± standard deviation (SD).

figures.label: Figure 7
figures.caption: Percentage cell viability calculated from electrochemical and spectrophotometric MTS measurements following chemical exposure after a 3-h incubation with the MTS reagent(A) Viability in hDFs and (B) viability in N/TERT-1 keratinocytes. Viability was normalized with PBS (negative control) set at 100% and SDS 5% aq. (positive control) at 0%. No statistically significant differences (ns) were observed between the electrochemical and colorimetric methods for most conditions, except for 5% KOH in hDFs, which showed statistical significance (∗∗p < 0.01, as determined by two-way ANOVA). Data are represented as mean ± standard deviation (SD) for n = 7 replicates.

figures.label: Figure 8
figures.caption: Evaluation of the methodology for a complex epithelial tissue(A) Percentage viability of reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) models after chemical exposure, calculated from both electrochemical and spectrophotometric MTS measurements. Viability was normalized to the negative control (PBS), set as 100%. Chemicals tested include PBS (C−), 5% aq. SDS (C+), 1-bromo-4-chlorobutane, 1-decanol, HCl, sulfuric acid, 5% aq. KOH, and isopropanol. Data are represented as mean ± standard deviation (SD) for n = 3 replicates. Red dashed line indicates IC50 as 50% of viability for chemical corrosive and irritation assessment. Statistical significance for comparison between electrochemical and colorimetric methods for each chemical: no significance (ns), p value < 0.001 (∗∗∗).(B) Histological characterization of the RHE model. Representative H&E stained section of the reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) used for electrochemical validation. The image confirms the presence of a fully stratified epithelium, including a prominent stratum corneum (SC), granular layer, and basal layer. This complex architecture demonstrates the robustness of the electrochemical MTS assay in monitoring viability within a highly organized 3D barrier model. Scale bars, 50 μm.
